records.name: Stenton, NSCDA/PA
records.summary: The Stenton historic house museum in North Philadelphia, run by the Colonial Dames of America in Pennsylvania. It offers timed house tours, history talks and seasonal family events, such as a fall harvest festival.
records.what_you_do: Book a timed house tour, come to a history talk or a family event such as the Halloween Harvest Festival, or support the Friends of Stenton. Volunteer roles are not listed on the site.

schedule.text: Timed house tours run Tuesday to Saturday from April 1 to December 19, starting on the hour from 1 to 3 pm. Second Saturdays are open 12 to 4 pm, May through October. From January to March, visits are by appointment.

cost.text: Adult admission is $10, and students, children and seniors pay $8. Children under 6 are free, and so are Friends of Stenton members and residents of zip codes 19140, 19141 and 19144. Some events, such as the fall symposium, have their own ticket prices.

access.notes: Nearest SEPTA: Wayne Junction station on the Regional Rail, about four blocks away. Bus 23 stops at Windrim and Germantown Avenues, and Logan station on the Broad Street Line is a walk away.

first_step.how: Book a timed house tour by calling 215-329-7312 or emailing programs@stenton.org. A booking guarantees your place.
first_step.basis: Tours and many events are open to the public and have a phone and email way to book. The site does not describe a newcomer program.
first_step.what_to_expect: Expect a timed walk through the historic house, booked ahead by phone or email. The site does not say how long a tour takes or who leads it. Adult admission is $10, with lower prices for students, children and seniors.
first_visit_tips: Reserve a spot on a timed tour, since a booking guarantees your place.
Arrive a few minutes before the hour, when tours start.
Take the Regional Rail to Wayne Junction, about four blocks away, or bus 23 to Windrim and Germantown Avenues.
Check the programs page before you visit, since the site lists holiday closures and changed hours.

records.notes: Tier 1 said second Saturday tours are free and listed tours at 12, 1, 2 and 3 pm. The visit page gives $10 adult admission, does not say second Saturdays are free, and starts tours on the hour at 1, 2 and 3 pm. Cost and tour times now follow the visit page. The 12 pm start appears only on the October 10 event. Not on the site: how long a tour runs, who leads tours, whether walk-ins are accepted, parking, and ramps or restrooms. Dated 2026 and 2027 programs are kept out of schedule text.

records.name: Stonewall Sports Philadelphia
records.summary: A recreational sports and social group for the LGBTQIA+ community. It runs leagues in sports such as kickball, volleyball, bowling and pickleball, plus trivia and social events.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a league as a player, on a team, as a free agent or as a small group, or come to new member mixers and community events.

schedule.text: Leagues run in seasons, with sign ups before each season. The pages checked do not list league days or times.

cost.text: The league pages do not list fees. The Player Assistance Fund can waive league registration fees in full or in part for people facing financial hardship, and it takes applications before each season's registration.

first_step.how: Subscribe to the monthly updates, then register for a league through the league registration page when a season opens. Winter 2027 sign ups are expected in mid-November.
first_step.basis: The site runs new member calls and mixers each season, offers free agent teams for first-time league players, and says no athletic experience is needed. Drop in is not described, so the group is not rated higher.
first_step.what_to_expect: The group says no athletic experience is needed. New players can register as free agents, and free agent teams are made up of other new players, so everyone starts at the same point. New member calls and mixers each season help people meet others and learn how the leagues run.
first_visit_tips: If you do not have a team, pick the free agent option so the group can match you by skill and interest.
Subscribe to the monthly updates so you hear when registration opens.
Email info@stonewallphilly.org with questions about fees or a specific league.
If cost is a concern, look into the Player Assistance Fund before you register.

records.notes: The leagues page lists eight leagues plus leagues for women, trans and non-binary players, but shows no days, times, venues or fees. The events calendar is an embedded Google Calendar with no dates in the page text, so it was not used. The running group named in tier 1 does not appear on the pages checked, so the summary no longer names it. The newest dated item is the Fall 2026 registration close in August 2026.

records.name: Sub & Surface Club (Toastmasters club 00002886)
records.summary: A Toastmasters club that meets at noon at the Navy Yard in South Philadelphia, in person or online, to practice public speaking. Visits are free, and guests do not have to speak until they feel ready.
records.what_you_do: Practice short speeches at lunchtime meetings, and take meeting roles such as timer or evaluator.

schedule.text: 2nd and 4th Wednesdays, noon to 1 pm, in person at the Navy Yard or online through Google Meet.

locations.label: The Navy Yard (entrance at the leasing office, reached from Chapel Way)

cost.text: Visits are free. Dues are not shown on the club site or the Toastmasters listing.

first_step.how: Use the club's online contact form to say you want to visit, then come to a noon meeting at the Navy Yard or join online through Google Meet.
first_step.basis: Guests are welcome at any upcoming meeting, the first meeting is free, and the Toastmasters listing says there is no pressure to take part until a guest is ready.
first_step.what_to_expect: A meeting runs about an hour at noon. Members give prepared and impromptu speeches, practice meeting roles, and give each other feedback. Guests are welcome to sit in, and a guest does not have to speak until ready.
first_visit_tips: Enter through the leasing office, reached from Chapel Way between Constitution Avenue and Normandy Place.
To join online, use Google Meet; the club's directions page has the link.
The club pages do not list parking or transit, so ask through the contact form before you come.
Arrive a few minutes early so you can find the entrance.

records.notes: The meetings page says no upcoming meetings are published yet, so the status stays probably_active with no dated evidence. The directions page suggests emailing an address for entrance and parking questions, but the contact page calls that address automated, so this record points to the contact form instead. The phone number comes from the Toastmasters listing, since the club site shows none. The Google Meet link is not recorded here.

records.name: Swim Pony Performing Arts
records.summary: A Philadelphia theatre company that makes immersive and playful devised shows, including interactive work that takes place in unusual spaces.
records.what_you_do: Come to one of the company's immersive shows, or support the company with a donation through its Can I Help page. The site lists no volunteer roles, classes or workshops.

schedule.text: The site does not show a regular schedule or dates for its productions.

cost.text: Ticket prices are not shown on the site.

first_step.how: Send a message through the site's contact form to ask about the next show, since the site shows no dates or ticket page.
first_step.basis: Shows are open to the public, but the site shows no dates, ticket page or prices, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The shows are immersive, playful devised pieces, and some are set in unusual places. The site does not say how long a show runs, where it is staged, or what it costs, so ask before you plan a visit.
first_visit_tips: Use the contact form to ask for the next show date and ticket details.
Expect a show rather than a class, since the site lists no classes or workshops.
If you want to support the company, the Can I Help page offers a donation link.

records.notes: Eight productions are listed with no dates, venues or prices. The site has no classes, workshops or ticket page. The Can I Help page offers only donations, through a fiscal sponsor, so the tier 1 wording about volunteering was corrected. Status is set to unknown rather than probably_active: the homepage is live and features a new show with no date, but the newest dated items on the site are from 2014 to 2016 (the Cross Pollination archive). One web search for 2026 shows found nothing from the company, and the most recent dated work it reported was from 2020. Reviewer: consider dormant or hide unless 2025 or 2026 activity is confirmed.

records.name: Friends of Tacony Creek Park
records.summary: Neighbors and visitors who look after Tacony Creek Park, a 300-acre watershed park in lower Northeast Philadelphia. The group runs free group walks and runs on the trails.
records.what_you_do: Join a free group walk or run on the trails, or volunteer for park cleanups, planting days and storm drain marking through the online form.

schedule.text: Weekly group walks and runs, called Walk with Me and Run with Me, plus other trail programs. The Friends site points to a partner events calendar for days and times.

access.notes: A 3.2-mile paved trail runs the length of the park for walking, running and biking. It is open from dawn to dusk.

first_step.how: Come to a Walk with Me or Run with Me, using the date and meeting time from the partner events calendar, or fill in the volunteer form to join a cleanup or planting day.
first_step.basis: The walks are free and open to visitors, and the site lists a volunteer form and a contact form. The site does not say beginners are welcome by name.
first_step.what_to_expect: The walks and runs are free and happen weekly on the park trails. The Friends site does not list meeting points, distances or paces, so check the events calendar first. For volunteer days, you fill in the online form, and someone from the group contacts you after you submit.
first_visit_tips: Check the events calendar for the walk's meeting point, time and distance before you go.
Take a SEPTA bus to a neighborhood gateway. The park's interactive map shows the closest one, and buses 18 and 26 stop at some gateways.
Watch your footing on the narrow, curved trail. In an emergency, call 911 and give the nearest gateway or intersection.
Send questions through the Contact Us form on the Friends site.

records.notes: Walk days, times, meeting points and distances are on the partner events calendar at ttfwatershed.org/events, which the Friends events page links to. That calendar was not read because this group reached its six-fetch limit, so the schedule stays general. The email address comes from the city registry, since the Friends site has only forms. The last_sign_of_life of 2026-10 is carried over from tier 1 and was not re-verified; the Friends pages show no dated items. The partner's reporting line, 215-744-1853, is not recorded as a group contact.

records.name: Tacony LAB Community Art Center
records.summary: A community art center in Tacony that is a program of Mural Arts Philadelphia, run in partnership with the local city council office. It offers free art classes, an open studio, and art clubs for kids and teens.
records.what_you_do: Take a free painting, drawing, sewing, weaving or laser cutter class, or use the open studio.

schedule.text: The open studio runs more than 30 hours a week. Posted hours: Monday noon to 8 pm, Tuesday 10 am to 8 pm, Wednesday 4 to 8 pm, Thursday noon to 4 pm and Friday 10 am to 2 pm. Saturdays are open only during kids classes, and the center is closed Sunday.

cost.text: Art classes are free. Many events need advance registration, and most event listings do not show a price.

first_step.how: Walk into the open studio during posted hours, or register for a free class or event through the events page, which uses Eventbrite.
first_step.basis: Classes are free, the open studio runs posted hours, and the monthly open sew says no experience is needed. Many events need advance registration, so the group is not rated 5.
first_step.what_to_expect: The open studio is for working on a project you bring or starting a new one. Classes are free and cover painting, drawing, sewing, weaving and laser cutter design. The page does not say how long a class runs or who attends.
first_visit_tips: Bring a project to work on, or come ready to start something new.
Check the events page first, since many events need an advance sign up.
Call (267) 686-7420 or email info@taconylab.org with questions about classes.

records.notes: The events page names Eventbrite as the registration platform; Eventbrite itself was not read. Wheelchair access is stated on the homepage intro, while the visit page is silent on it. The events page lists 2026 events, including a kids art club for ages 6 to 18 and a family art club for ages 2 and up, but those dated items are kept out of schedule text. The page does not say which kids club runs on Saturdays, so those details stay general. Languages spoken, parking and transit are not stated. Tier 1 had no zip; the visit page gives 19135. Mural Arts Philadelphia is the parent program, but no link to it appears on the page, so it is not in leads_only.

records.name: Tai Chi in the Square (Franklin Square Tai Chi Group)
records.summary: A free morning tai chi group that practices outdoors at Franklin Square, open to everyone.
records.what_you_do: Practice tai chi outdoors with the group, and move to the pavilion when the weather is cold or wet.

schedule.text: Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays, 7:30 to 8:30 am.

locations.label: Franklin Square, northeast side of the fountain

first_step.how: Go to the northeast side of the fountain at Franklin Square at 7:30 am on a Tuesday, Thursday or Saturday.
first_step.basis: The page says all are welcome at a set place and time, and it describes no sign up. It does not say beginners are welcome by name, and it describes no newcomer program.
first_step.what_to_expect: A free outdoor tai chi session from 7:30 to 8:30 am, with the group gathered at the northeast side of the fountain. The page does not name a leader or describe the class format. On cold, rainy or snowy days, the group moves to the pavilion in the northwest part of the square.
first_visit_tips: Arrive a few minutes before 7:30 am and look for the group by the fountain.
On cold, wet or snowy mornings, look for the group at the pavilion in the northwest part of the square.
Dress for the weather in clothes you can move in.
For updates, the group's Facebook group is the listed way to join.

records.notes: Only one page covers this group: a Historic Philadelphia event listing, which is a host page rather than the group's own site. The group's Facebook group was not read, since it is a lead-only platform. The Historic Philadelphia home page has no tai chi listing. The event page shows no start or end date. The only 2026 is in the footer copyright, which is not used as evidence. The site had no more detail than tier 1, beyond the drop in and what to expect text.
